newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds continued to slip on Tuesday and ended well down, as the dollar's strength against the guilder and the mark spooked the market.

At 1540 GMT, the dollar stood at 2.0283/93 per 100 guilders, and although the recent firming of the U.S. currency would probably not prompt a hike in Germany's repo rate, dealers said it had caused a dent in the bond market for the day.
"People talk about the dollar strength, and no doubt it's caused part of the (September Bund) futures' drop, but it's too early for an interest rate rise," one dealer said.

"A hike of the repo would give a strong, wrong signal to the market...and besides, the Buba doesn't practise an exchange rate policy but screens M3 and inflation for that," ING Barings economist Arthur Rasmussen said.
He said the German recovery was still too weak to justify a German rate hike this year, adding there was no fear for inflation either.
The 0.5 percent U.S. June retail sales growth, well above the expected 0.2 rise, also pressured bonds, dealers said.
The long bond, maturing in January 2023 ended down 38 basis points at 114.53/73 bid/ask for a bid yield of 6.33 percent.
Dealers said the February 2007 benchmark performed relatively well, as it closed off 19 basis points at 101.41/49, yielding 5.55 percent at bid.
They said professional trades dominated the market, adding they had not seen any big switching along the yield curve or with Germany. The yield gaps with Bunds were broadly unchanged.
"But the market is quite volatile at the moment, so it is difficult to detect trends," one of them said.
Dealers said long term market sentiment remained fine, supported by the slow German pick-up and confidence in EMU.
But on the short term, bonds might drop further, they said.
"We've crossed the 102.30 support in the (Bund) future and if the dollar stays this strong, it wouldn't surprise me if we went down to 102.00 the next couple of days ," one dealer said.
Another said he expected the Bund future to hold above its next support, which he saw at 102.17.
